beat1_summary: Awareness held and conversion got better. What changed is the middle: fewer people commented, saved or watched all the way through, even though the ones who did convert more efficiently than any account we run.
work_chips: Themes: custom pieces, the Cincy tennis story, in-store events
Focus: bringing people to the shop
beat2_takeaway: We published 8 pieces in August, three Reels and five carousels, weighted toward the custom work and the local stories.
beat3_takeaway: Almost one in five people who saw your profile tapped through, the best click-through rate in our book. The gap is one step earlier: fewer people commented, saved or finished a video before getting there.
beat4_takeaway: Your most-shared piece was a carousel, not a Reel. The gold-moments set travelled 5.6 times further than an average post, so the format is reaching people. It is the response it invites that changed.
beat5_takeaway: September is about giving people something to respond to. Conversion is already the strongest in our book, so the work is one step earlier: content that earns a comment and a save, not just a click.

goal_narratives: Awareness scored 42%, close to level with July. Shares and views held inside your Lift range and new followers ticked up, so reach is broadly steady.

Engagement scored 18%, the band that moved. Comments came down from 70 to 18 and saves to 32, with retention easing to 24%. This is the step the September work is aimed at, because engagement is also what Instagram reads when it decides how far to push a post.
Conversion scored 70%, up from July and the strongest part of your funnel. Click-through hit 18.5%, well above the Lift ceiling, and bio link taps rose to 160.
